_readme: Merge into <content-repo>/.claude/settings.json. Replace //c/<content-repo> with the repo's absolute path (on Windows write //<drive>/<path>; paths are normalised to POSIX) and <equipment> with each equipment name registered in plug.yaml.
deny only understands Edit(path) / Read(path): a Write(path) rule is accepted but never checked, so it does nothing. An Edit rule covers every built-in file-editing tool, Write included.
Never deny Read(self/RULES.md): the pilot has to be able to read the rules. Read() is only for things it should neither read nor change (the hooks' last-fired stamps).

deny rules cover self/ and the equipment registered in plug.yaml. work/, workshop/ and any unregistered directory under tools/ are deliberately left writable — that is where products and new equipment are built.
deny applies in every mode, bypassPermissions included; it cannot stop a script writing directly (native Windows has no sandbox) — the backstop is gates/precommit.py.

These rules bind a session whose project root is this content repo. An agent working from another root edits these files unimpeded and is only stopped at commit time by pre-commit; plug check --contact proves the rules are written, not that they are in force.
Replace the paths in the hook commands with wherever you cloned entryplug. Installing as a plugin uses hooks/hooks.json instead (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}).
`plug init --pilot claude-code` writes all of this for you, with real absolute paths, merged and idempotent.
